paper.title: Cascading Bandits: Learning to Rank in the Cascade Model

unmapped: Item attraction weights are independent Bernoulli across items and time (Assumption 1); reward is 1 - prod(1 - w(a_k)), i.e. at least one attractive item in the list
Paper's L (number of items) is canonical K; paper's K (list length) is canonical m
Optimal solution as a set is unique
settings.definition_quote: we represent the problem by a tuple $B = (E, P, K)$, where $E = \set{1, \dots, L}$ is a ground set of $L$ items, $P$ is a probability distribution over a unit hypercube $\set{0, 1}^E$, and $K \leq L$ is the number of recommended items. ... The weights $w$ are distributed as: $P(w) = \prod_{e \in E} P_e(w(e))$, where $P_e$ is a Bernoulli distribution with mean $\bar{w}(e)$.

symbols.Delta_eK: gap between the m-th most attractive item and suboptimal item e: wbar(m) - wbar(e)

tuning: initialized with one sample w_0 (O(K) steps)

source.label: thm:ucb1
source.quote: The expected $n$-step regret of $\cascadeucb$ is bounded as: R(n) \leq \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{12}{\Delta_{e, K}} \log n + \frac{\pi^2}{3} L.

results.notes: Paper's L = canonical K (items), paper's K = m (list length); sum is over the K-m suboptimal items. Regret defined via expected reward f(A*,w)-f(A_t,w) = pseudo-regret.

bound.expression_latex: \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, K} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, K}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(K)}} (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C,\ C = K L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 K \log \log n

symbols.Delta_eK: wbar(m) - wbar(e) for suboptimal item e

tuning: exploration level log t + 3 log log t

source.label: thm:klucb
source.quote: For any $\eps > 0$, the expected $n$-step regret of $\cascadeklucb$ is bounded as: R(n) \leq \sum_{e = K + 1}^L \frac{(1 + \eps) \Delta_{e, K} (1 + \log(1 / \Delta_{e, K}))}{\kl{\bar{w}(e)}{\bar{w}(K)}} \times (\log n + 3 \log \log n) + C, where $C = K L \frac{C_2(\eps)}{n^{\beta(\eps)}} + 7 K \log \log n$...

results.notes: Paper's K -> m, paper's L -> K. Constants C_2, beta defined in cited work.

symbols.p_attr: attraction probability of each optimal item in the hard instance B_LB

conditions: instance B_LB(L,K,p,Delta): optimal items have attraction p, suboptimal items p - Delta, Delta in (0,p)

source.label: thm:lower bound
source.quote: For any cascading bandit $B_\mathrm{LB}$, the regret of any consistent algorithm is bounded from below as: \liminf_{n \to \infty} \frac{R(n)}{\log n} \geq \frac{(L - K) \Delta (1 - p)^{K - 1}}{\kl{p - \Delta}{p}}.

results.notes: Paper's L -> K, paper's K -> m. Consistent: E[T_n(A)] = o(n^alpha) for any suboptimal list.
